newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's petrochem sector improved in Q4 - chamber.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's petrochem sector improved in Q4 - chamber.

text.p: Mexico's chemical sector saw moderate growth in 1996 and expects continued improvements in 1997, the National Chemical Industry Association (ANIQ) said Tuesday in a report.

The sector improved its installed capacity levels by seven percent to 77 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. Chamber members said in a recent survey they expect improved production to continue in 1997.

"In congruence with the good behavior registered in 1996 for the world chemicals industry, Mexican businesses in the sector reported good results, which without being as spectacular as 1995, were still positive," the ANIQ report said.

The report said the ANIQ's members expect improved sales in 1997 partly due to a history of higher consumption in federal election years. Congressional and mayoral elections are scheduled for early July.
"For the first quarter of 1997, the sector's production will present general increases in the order of five percent," the report said, noting output in certain resins is projected at 10 percent.

Production of adhesives, lubricants and chemical products for construction grew a respective 12 percent, 17 percent and nine percent in 1996. The report said smallest growth was seen in agrochemicals, artificial fibers, synthetics, fertilizers and petrochemicals, which grew between one and five percent.

As domestic recovery continued to lag with chemicals sales up 12.5 percent, the ANIQ said chemicals most exported, such as emulsions, pigments, colorings, adhesives and articial and synthetic fibers, grew at least 18 percent.

Mexico continued to be a net importer of chemicals, the report said. Chemicals exports totalled $3.47 billion and imports reached $5.694 million, for a negative trade balance in the sector of $2.224 billion.
"Of this amount, $382 million corresponded to imports of products elaborated by Pemex (state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos), whose supply is insufficient," the ANIQ wrote.
The exchange rate's stability has reduced the sector's competitiveness in exports, ANIQ said.
